test_case.description: Fault injection — simulate scheduler stall and verify watchdog latches the motor driver
test_case.setup: Pump in standard infusion mode; instrumented build with a debug hook to suspend the rate-control task indefinitely.
test_case.steps: 1. Start an infusion at 5 mL/hr. 2. Trigger the debug hook to suspend the rate-control task. 3. Observe the watchdog timer and motor driver state. 4. Observe the UI banner.
test_case.expectedResults: 1. Watchdog counter stalls as expected. 2. After 200 ms, the motor driver latches to the safe state and stops issuing pulses. 3. The UI renders the Alarm Mode banner and silences the nominal-rate display.

requirements.text: The rate-control loop shall be monitored by an independent hardware watchdog. The motor driver shall be latched into a safe (no-pulse) state if a heartbeat from the rate-control task is missed for more than 200 ms.
The UI thread shall render an Alarm Mode banner and silence nominal-rate displays when the rate-control task heartbeat is missed for more than 200 ms.

design_docs.name: Rate Control Loop and Watchdog Architecture
design_docs.description: Describes the segregation of the rate-control task from the UI task, the heartbeat protocol, the hardware watchdog wiring, and the safe-state latch behavior of the motor driver. Documents the 200 ms timeout threshold and the fail-safe state machine that transitions the motor driver to no-pulse mode when heartbeats are missed.

design_docs.name: Hardware Watchdog Interface Design
design_docs.description: Specifies the hardware watchdog timer interface, including the GPIO pin assignments for heartbeat signals, the watchdog timer configuration (200 ms timeout), and the motor driver latch control signals. Documents the electrical characteristics of the safe-state latch circuit.

design_docs.name: UI Alarm Mode Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the UI alarm rendering logic, including the state machine that monitors the rate-control task heartbeat, the Alarm Mode banner component, and the logic that silences nominal-rate displays when the alarm is active. Documents the UI thread's dependency on the same heartbeat signal monitored by the hardware watchdog.

test_case.description: Verify MFA enforcement cannot be bypassed by direct URL navigation.
test_case.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user has valid credentials but has not completed MFA.
test_case.steps:
Step: 1. Complete first-factor authentication (password only).
Step: 2. Capture the session token from browser cookies.
Step: 3. Attempt to navigate directly to the EHR dashboard URL without completing MFA.
Step: 4. Observe the system response.
test_case.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Password authentication succeeds and MFA prompt is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. Session token is captured but marked as 'MFA_PENDING'.
ExpectedResult: 3. System intercepts the direct navigation attempt.
ExpectedResult: 4. User is redirected back to the MFA prompt page with message 'Multi-factor authentication required'.

requirements.text: The EHR system shall enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing patient health information (PHI), requiring both a password and a time-based one-time password (TOTP) token generated by an authenticator app.
The EHR system shall prevent unauthorized access to PHI by enforcing MFA completion before granting access to any PHI-containing routes, including direct URL navigation attempts.

design_docs.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Architecture
design_docs.description: Describes the two-phase authentication flow: first-factor (password) validation against the user database, followed by second-factor (TOTP) validation using the HMAC-based One-Time Password algorithm (RFC 6238). Documents the session state machine that tracks MFA completion status and prevents bypass via direct URL navigation.

design_docs.name: Session Management Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the session token lifecycle, including the MFA_PENDING state that is set after first-factor authentication and cleared only after successful TOTP validation. Documents the middleware that intercepts all PHI-accessing routes and enforces MFA completion before granting access.

design_docs.name: Authentication Middleware Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the Express.js middleware stack that intercepts all incoming HTTP requests, validates session tokens, checks MFA completion status, and redirects unauthenticated or MFA-incomplete requests to the appropriate authentication pages. Documents the route protection logic and the whitelist of public routes that bypass MFA enforcement.

test_case.description: Verify video quality does NOT restore to HD if bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second stabilization period completes.
test_case.setup: Telemedicine video module active; video call in SD mode; network throttling tool configured.
test_case.steps:
Step: 1. Verify current video resolution is 640x480.
Step: 2. Increase bandwidth to 2.5 Mbps.
Step: 3. After 5 seconds, drop bandwidth to 1.8 Mbps.
Step: 4. Observe video stream quality.
test_case.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video resolution is 640x480.
ExpectedResult: 2. Bandwidth increases above 2.0 Mbps.
ExpectedResult: 3. Bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second timer completes.
ExpectedResult: 4. Video stream remains in SD mode (640x480); no upgrade to HD occurs.

requirements.text: The telemedicine video consultation module shall automatically degrade the video stream quality from HD (1280x720) to SD (640x480) when the detected network bandwidth drops below 1.5 Mbps, and shall restore HD quality when bandwidth recovers above 2.0 Mbps for at least 10 consecutive seconds.

design_docs.name: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming Design
design_docs.description: Describes the adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm that monitors network bandwidth via WebRTC statistics and dynamically adjusts video encoding parameters. Documents the hysteresis logic that prevents rapid oscillation between HD and SD modes: degradation threshold at 1.5 Mbps (immediate), restoration threshold at 2.0 Mbps (with 10-second stabilization timer).

design_docs.name: Bandwidth Monitoring Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the bandwidth monitoring service that polls WebRTC getStats() API every 1 second, calculates the rolling average bandwidth over the last 5 seconds, and triggers quality adjustment events when thresholds are crossed. Documents the 10-second stabilization timer implementation that prevents premature HD restoration.

design_docs.name: Video Quality State Machine Detailed Design
design_docs.description: Detailed design of the video quality state machine with three states: HD_ACTIVE, SD_ACTIVE, and HD_PENDING (during the 10-second stabilization period). Documents the state transition logic, the timer management, and the event handlers that respond to bandwidth threshold crossings.
